claims.text: A high-entropy spinel oxide can contain Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn.
Solventless thermolysis can be used to synthesize the proposed seven-metal high-entropy spinel oxide.
Solventless thermolysis followed by calcination at approximately 600 °C in air will produce a thin, uniform high-entropy oxide coating on high-surface-area alumina.
Pt can be deposited evenly on the coated support at less than 50% of conventional Pt loading.
Adhesion promoters or graded interfaces will offset thermal mismatch during repeated high-temperature cycling.
The disordered multi-metal spinel layer enhances oxygen mobility.
The spinel layer creates an active lattice-oxygen network at the Pt/support interface.
The spinel layer mediates strong metal-support interactions with Pt.
The high-entropy spinel layer inhibits Pt sintering.
Greater configurational disorder in spinel oxides improves CO oxidation activity.
Configurational disorder increases lattice-oxygen participation in oxidation reactions.
Increased lattice-oxygen participation lowers the activation barrier for CO oxidation.
Increased lattice-oxygen participation lowers the activation barrier for hydrocarbon oxidation.
The oxide interface stabilizes Pt nanoparticles against sintering and deactivation during prolonged thermal cycling.
The modified Pt/high-entropy-oxide/alumina catalyst will have a lower CO light-off temperature than conventional Pt/alumina.
The modified catalyst will have a lower hydrocarbon light-off temperature than conventional Pt/alumina.
The modified catalyst will sustain catalytic activity over extended automotive-exhaust operation.
Reducing Pt loading to less than 50% of conventional levels will not compromise catalyst durability.
Insufficient adhesion between the high-entropy oxide and alumina will degrade performance under thermal cycling.
